ambiguous_groups_now_reported.note: No correspondence is asserted for these. The positional-pairing sensitivity, labelled algorithm-dependent, would put agreement at 85.40% (entry DOI) and 85.27% (surrogate) if they were paired greedily -- which is why they must not be blended into the headline rate.

direction_of_the_change: Identifier agreement rose, from 96.91% to 99.87% for the entry DOI and from 95.26% to 99.87% for the surrogate. The old figure UNDERSTATED agreement on the forced-correspondence population, because it folded in ambiguous groups where it had paired records arbitrarily -- and all 1,673 ambiguous groups contain candidates whose identifiers disagree, so those arbitrary pairings were counted as disagreements. Blending the two populations was the error; the corrected figures report them apart.

moved_on_a_non_publication_slot_field.old: 484 implied by 30,699 - 30,215, an artifact of the broken pairing

positional_pairing_sensitivity.method: lexicographic greedy pairing of sorted removal records against sorted addition records within each ambiguous group, consuming counts
positional_pairing_sensitivity.status: ALGORITHM-DEPENDENT, not evidence about any individual observation

what_the_old_number_actually_was: 30,699 was the count of removal OCCURRENCES sitting in a group that had at least one eligible addition -- not the count of matched pairs. It equals the corrected removal-occurrences-considered figure exactly, which is how the defect was confirmed: the old code counted every such removal and let additions be reused.
why: The first cross-slot analysis had two defects. It matched a removal against an addition without consuming the addition's count, so two removals sharing a key both counted as moves into one addition. And it took the first eligible addition in file order, so reversing the detail file changed which record a removal was compared against, and with it the reported identifier agreement. Both are reproduced as regression tests in tests/test_m11d_cross_slot_pairing.py.
